mainTopic: The crossing of the ירדן: how high the water piled up, what יהושע told the people in the river, the memorial stones, and the weight of the מרגלים' grape cluster
overview: The גמרא describes the crossing of the ירדן. The moment the feet of the כהנים touched the water, the river stopped and piled up. רבי יהודה says the heap was 12 מיל, the size of the camp of ישראל. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון objects that water moves faster than people and would have flooded them, so he says it piled up more than 300 מיל, high enough for kings everywhere to see. He supports this from פסוקים about the kings' terror and from רחב's words. Next comes a series of things יהושע said while the people stood in the river: a warning that the water could return and sweep away 'me and you,' and instructions about memorial stones. A report that each stone weighed about forty סאה, combined with a tradition about carrying, lets the גמרא work out the weight of the מרגלים' grape cluster. רבי יצחק adds that eight spies carried it, and that יהושע and כלב carried nothing. The amud ends as רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא begin to disagree about the water dispute, and their argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The water stops when the priests' feet touch it
steps.stepSummary: Once the feet of the כהנים touched the ירדן, the water turned back and stood in a heap, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: As soon as the feet of the כהנים dipped into the water, the water flowed backward. The פסוק says: 'When those carrying the ארון came to the ירדן, the waters coming down from above stood still and rose up in one heap.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes the miracle at the ירדן and backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is timing. The water stopped at the exact moment the כהנים carrying the ארון stepped in, not before. The פסוק's words 'קמו נד אחד' (rose up in one heap) set up the next question: how tall was that heap?

keyTerms.meaning: one heap / one wall of water

phrases.english: And once the feet of the priests were dipped in the water,
the water went back on itself,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּכְבוֹא נוֹשְׂאֵי הָאָרוֹן עַד הַיַּרְדֵּן וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: as it says: 'And when those carrying the Ark came to the Jordan, etc.'
'and the waters coming down from above stood still,'
'they rose up in one heap.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier description of the crossing of the ירדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ירדן stopped and piled up the moment the כהנים' feet touched the water.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the water rose twelve מיל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the heap of water was 12 מיל by 12 מיל, matching the size of the camp of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: How tall was the water? Twelve מיל by twelve מיל, matching the camp of ישראל. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how high the heap of water was, and רבי יהודה gives a measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ties the size of the heap to the size of the camp of ישראל, which was 12 מיל. His logic is that the miracle was exactly as big as it needed to be for the people to cross. This is the view that the next step will attack.

keyTerms.meaning: a measure of distance, about a kilometer
the camp of the Jewish people
these are the words of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: And how high was the water?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִיל עַל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִיל,
phrases.english: Twelve mil by twelve mil,
matching the camp of Israel.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Measures the heap described in the פסוק of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the water piled up 12 מיל, matching the camp of ישראל.

steps.title: Water moves faster than people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון challenges רבי יהודה: water is faster than people, so a 12-מיל heap would flood them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון said to him: According to you, which is faster, a person or water? You must say water is faster. If so, the water would come and wash them away!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון attacks רבי יהודה's measurement with a logical argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He sets up a simple comparison: water moves faster than people walk. If the heap were only as big as the camp, the water would rush over before the whole nation finished crossing and sweep them away. So 12 מיל cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: you must say / the answer has to be

steps.confusionAlert: Here קל does not mean 'light' or 'easy'. It means 'quick'. The question is which moves faster, people or water.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לִדְבָרֶיךָ, אָדָם קַל, אוֹ מַיִם קַלִּים?
phrases.english: According to you, is a person faster, or is water faster?
You have to say: water is faster.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, בָּאִין מַיִם וְשׁוֹטְפִין אוֹתָן!
phrases.english: If so, the water would come and wash them away!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לִדְבָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי יהודה's 12-מיל measurement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the heap was only 12 מיל high.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water moves faster than people, so a heap only as big as the camp would overflow onto the people before they finished crossing.

steps.title: The water piled up over three hundred מיל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון gives his own view: the water piled up in heaps more than 300 מיל high, until kings East and West saw it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches that the water gathered and rose in heaps upon heaps, more than three hundred מיל, until all the kings of the East and West saw it.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבי יהודה's number, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון offers his own picture of the miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A much taller heap solves the problem from step 3, because the water would not reach the people while they crossed. It also adds something new: the miracle was big enough to be seen far away by kings in every direction. The next step will prove this from a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches that the water was heaped up
and rising in heaps upon heaps,
more than three hundred mil,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁרָאוּ אוֹתָן כׇּל מַלְכֵי מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב,
phrases.english: until all the kings of the East and West saw it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי יהודה's measurement after the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the challenged view with a new measurement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The heap was only as big as the camp, 12 מיל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The heap was more than 300 מיל high, so it could not flood the people and was visible to far-off kings.

steps.title: Proof: the kings heard and their hearts melted
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יהושע shows that all the Amorite and Canaanite kings heard about the drying of the ירדן and were terrified.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'When all the Amorite kings beyond the ירדן westward, and all the Canaanite kings by the sea, heard that God had dried up the ירדן before בני ישראל until they crossed, their hearts melted, and there was no spirit left in them because of בני ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון brings a פסוק to support his claim that faraway kings knew about the miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names kings on different sides, beyond the ירדן and by the sea, and says all of them were struck with fear. That fits a heap of water so tall that it could be noticed far away, as step 4 claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: their heart melted, they were terrified

phrases.english: as it says: 'And when all the kings of the Amorites heard,'
'who were across the Jordan to the west,'

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מַלְכֵי הַכְּנַעֲנִי אֲשֶׁר עַל הַיָּם
phrases.english: 'and all the kings of the Canaanites who were by the sea,'

phrases.aramaic: אֵת אֲשֶׁר הוֹבִישׁ ה׳ אֶת מֵי הַיַּרְדֵּן
phrases.english: 'that God had dried up the waters of the Jordan'
'before the children of Israel until they crossed,'

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּמַּס לְבָבָם וְלֹא הָיָה בָם עוֹד רוּחַ
phrases.english: 'their heart melted, and there was no more spirit in them'
'because of the children of Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיְהִי כִשְׁמֹעַ כׇּל מַלְכֵי הָאֱמֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4's claim that kings in every direction knew of the miracle.
steps.raayaObject: That the miracle reached the attention of kings East and West.

steps.title: רחב: the nations already trembled over ים סוף
steps.stepSummary: רחב told יהושע's spies that the people of כנען had heard about the splitting of ים סוף and their hearts melted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רחב the prostitute told יהושע's messengers: 'For we have heard how God dried up the water of ים סוף, etc.' And it is written: 'We heard, and our hearts melted, and no spirit remained, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second source, רחב's words, to show how strongly the nations reacted when they heard of such miracles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting ים סוף happened years earlier and far away, yet the people of כנען were still terrified. If a distant miracle frightened them that much, a huge miracle at the ירדן, right near them, would surely be seen and feared. This backs up רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's picture of the kings' terror.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says the water rose 12 מיל, the size of the camp. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says that would have flooded the people, so the water must have piled up more than 300 מיל, high enough for kings everywhere to see. The פסוקים about the kings' fear and רחב's words support his view.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה אָמְרָה לִשְׁלוּחֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: And even Rahab the prostitute said to Joshua's messengers:
'For we have heard how God dried up'
'the water of the Red Sea, etc.'
And it is written: 'We heard, and our hearts melted,'
'and no more spirit remained, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה אָמְרָה לִשְׁלוּחֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source about the nations' fear, strengthening step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the nations were deeply terrified by reports of such miracles.

steps.title: יהושע warns the people about why they are crossing
steps.stepSummary: Still standing in the ירדן, יהושע tells the people they are crossing in order to drive out the inhabitants of the land. If they do not, the water will sweep them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: While they were still in the ירדן, יהושע said: 'Know why you are crossing: to drive out the people of the land, as the פסוק says. If you do it, good. If not, the water will come and wash away אותיכם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new series of things יהושע said while the people were standing in the river. This is the first one: a warning with a condition attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle of the crossing comes with a condition. The people are crossing for a purpose, which is to inherit the land and drive out its inhabitants. If they fail to do that, the same water that stopped for them could come back down on them.

keyTerms.meaning: While they were still in the ירדן
On condition that, for the purpose of

phrases.english: While they were still in the Jordan, Yehoshua said to them:

phrases.aramaic: דְּעוּ עַל מָה אַתֶּם עוֹבְרִים אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן
phrases.english: Know for what purpose you are crossing the Jordan

phrases.aramaic: — עַל מְנָת שֶׁתּוֹרִישׁוּ אֶת יוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ מִפְּנֵיכֶם,
phrases.english: — in order that you drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּם אֶת כׇּל יוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ מִפְּנֵיכֶם וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'And you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, etc.'
If you do so — good.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו, בָּאִין מַיִם וְשׁוֹטְפִין אוֹתִיכֶם.
phrases.english: But if not, water will come and sweep away 'otichem.'
phrases.notes: אותיכם is an unusual word. The גמרא is about to explain it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the size of the water heap to what יהושע told the people while they stood in the ירדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The crossing was conditional on driving out the land's inhabitants; otherwise the waters would return and sweep them away.

steps.title: What does the word אותיכם mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the strange form of the word אותיכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does אותיכם mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about one odd word in יהושע's warning. This question sets up the explanation that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal word for 'you' would be אתכם. The longer form אותיכם seems to hint at something extra, so the גמרא asks what it means.

phrases.english: What is 'otichem'? —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in יהושע's warning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the unusual word אותיכם.

steps.title: אותיכם means 'me and you'
steps.stepSummary: The word is a blend of אותי (me) and אתכם (you). יהושע includes himself in the danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means 'me and you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word combines 'me' and 'you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By using this blended word, יהושע tells the people that if they fail, the water will sweep away him together with them. He does not stand apart from their fate.

phrases.english: Me and you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about אותיכם.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אותיכם is a blend of אותי and אתכם: יהושע includes himself in the warning.

steps.title: Carrying stones as a sign for the children
steps.stepSummary: יהושע's second instruction: each man lifts a stone on his shoulder, one for each שבט, as a sign for future generations that their fathers crossed the ירדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: While still in the ירדן, יהושע told them: 'Each man lift a stone onto his shoulder, by the number of the שבטים.' The פסוק adds that when your children ask what these stones are, they are a sign that the fathers crossed the ירדן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second thing יהושע said while the people were in the river. He gives them a physical reminder for the next generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא puts two פסוקים together. The first gives the command to carry stones, and the second gives the reason. The stones serve as a memorial so that children will ask about them and learn about the miracle.

phrases.english: While they were still in the Jordan, Yehoshua said to them:

phrases.aramaic: ״הָרִימוּ לָכֶם אִישׁ אֶבֶן אַחַת עַל שִׁכְמוֹ
phrases.english: 'Lift up, each man, one stone onto his shoulder
according to the number of the tribes of Israel, etc.'
And it is written: 'So that this will be a sign among you
when your children ask in the future, saying:
What are these stones to you? etc.'

phrases.aramaic: סִימָן לַבָּנִים שֶׁעָבְרוּ אָבוֹת אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן.
phrases.english: A sign for the children that the fathers crossed the Jordan.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹדָם בַּיַּרְדֵּן אָמַר לָהֶן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: ״הָרִימוּ לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second in the series of things יהושע said while in the ירדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stones carried on the shoulder serve as a sign to future generations of the crossing.

steps.title: Twelve stones from where the כהנים stood
steps.stepSummary: יהושע's third instruction: take twelve stones from the spot where the כהנים' feet stood in the ירדן, and set them down at the place where you sleep that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: While still in the ירדן, יהושע told them: 'Take twelve stones from the middle of the ירדן, from where the כהנים stood, carry them with you, and put them down at the place where you sleep tonight.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third thing יהושע said in the river. The גמרא quotes the פסוק and gets ready to clarify one detail in it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These stones come from a specific place, where the כהנים carrying the ארון stood. The פסוק says to set them down 'in the lodging place,' which raises a question about which lodging place is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place where the כהנים' feet stood
Lodging place, camping spot for the night

phrases.english: While they were still in the Jordan, Yehoshua said to them:
'Take for yourselves from here, from the middle of the Jordan,
from the place where the priests' feet stood firm,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אֲבָנִים וְהַעֲבַרְתֶּם אוֹתָם עִמָּכֶם
phrases.english: twelve stones, and carry them over with you
and set them down in the lodging place
where you will spend tonight, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹדָם בַּיַּרְדֵּן אָמַר לָהֶן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: ״שְׂאוּ לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third in the series of things יהושע said while in the ירדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twelve stones from where the כהנים stood were to be placed at the lodging place.

steps.title: Only that one night, not every stop
steps.stepSummary: One might think the stones had to be set up at every camping spot along the way. The words 'where you will spend tonight' show it was only that one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they had to put the stones down at every place they camped. That is why the פסוק says 'where you will spend tonight.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible misreading and then uses the exact words of the פסוק to rule it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the word 'tonight,' 'the lodging place' could mean every stop on their journey. The פסוק's exact wording limits the command to the first night after the crossing.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says (to teach otherwise)

phrases.english: One might think: at each and every lodging place —
therefore the verse says: 'where you will spend tonight.'

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל בְּכׇל מָלוֹן וּמָלוֹן — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the lodging-place instruction in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: That the stones were set down only at the first night's lodging place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words אשר תלינו בו הלילה in יהושע 4:3.

steps.title: Each stone weighed about forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports that three חכמים examined those stones and estimated that each one weighed about forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: אבא חלפתא, רבי אליעזר בן מתיא, and חנניא בן חכינאי stood at those stones and estimated that each one weighed about forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a report about how heavy the stones were. They were very heavy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each man carried one stone on his shoulder (step 10). So knowing the weight of a stone tells us how much each man lifted. This becomes the starting point for the calculation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of measure (volume or weight)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חֲלַפְתָּא וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן מַתְיָא
phrases.english: Abba Chalafta and Rabbi Eliezer ben Matya
and Chananya ben Chachinai
stood on those stones,
and estimated each and every one
weighed about forty se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fact about the stones described in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each stone taken from the ירדן weighed about forty סאה.

steps.title: A person lifts only a third of what he can carry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a known tradition: the load a person can lift onto his own shoulder is a third of the load he can carry when others help load it onto him.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a tradition that the load a person can lift onto his shoulder by himself is one third of what he can carry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a known rule about carrying. It is setting up a calculation, using the forty-סאה stones, of how much a person can really carry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man lifted a forty-סאה stone by himself, then by this rule he could carry three times that, 120 סאה, if others loaded it onto him. The rule turns the stone's weight into a measure of a person's full carrying strength.

phrases.english: And we have a tradition that a load
that a person lifts onto his own shoulder —
is a third of his full load.
phrases.notes: He means a person can carry three times as much when others put the load on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the rule needed to turn the stone's weight into a full carrying capacity.
steps.raayaObject: How much a person's full load is, based on what he can lift alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A received tradition (גמירי) about carrying loads.
steps.whatToRemember: Each stone was about forty סאה. Since a person lifts alone only a third of his full load, a man's full carrying strength was about three times that.

steps.title: The stone weights let us measure the grape cluster
steps.stepSummary: From the stone weights just given, we can calculate how heavy the מרגלים' grape cluster was, based on the פסוק 'they carried it on a pole between two.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From here you can figure out the weight of the grape cluster, as it says: 'And they carried it on a pole between two.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the stone numbers from the last two steps as a measuring tool for a different story, the grapes brought back by the מרגלים. This line sets up the reading of the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said one person lifted a 40 סאה stone onto his own shoulder. Step 14 said that with help, a person carries three times that much. So each carrier of the cluster could hold 120 סאה. Now we only need to know how many people carried it.

keyTerms.meaning: A pole used for carrying a load

phrases.english: From here you can calculate the cluster of grapes,
phrases.notes: 'From here' points back to the stone weights in steps 13 and 14.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And they carried it on a pole between two.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the weight figures from steps 13 and 14 to the grape cluster of the מרגלים.
steps.raayaObject: The weight of the grape cluster
steps.raayaSupportSource: The stone weights combined with the פסוק in במדבר 13:23

steps.title: Why does the פסוק add 'between two'?
steps.stepSummary: Anything carried on a pole needs two people anyway, so the word 'between two' seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it already says 'on a pole,' don't I already know it took two people? So why does the פסוק add 'between two'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a word in the פסוק that seems unnecessary and asks what it is there to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pole always has one person at each end, so 'on a pole' already means two people. The extra word 'between two' must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach? (Why is this word needed?)

phrases.english: From the fact that it says 'on a pole,'
don't I already know that it was carried by two?
What does the פסוק teach by saying 'between two'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 15.

steps.title: 'Between two' means two poles
steps.stepSummary: The extra word teaches that there were two poles, so four people carried the cluster.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means on two poles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'between two' refers to two poles, not two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two poles means four carriers. Each carrier could hold 120 סאה with help, so the cluster weighed 480 סאה. This finishes the calculation started in step 15.
steps.whatToRemember: Four carriers × 120 סאה each = a cluster of 480 סאה.

phrases.english: — on two poles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the poles were stacked on poles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the carrying setup was like stacked scale bars, a pole resting on poles, which means even more carriers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: it was like the bars of a scale, and bars resting on bars.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds a fuller picture of how the cluster was carried: poles laid on top of other poles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 pictured two poles with four people. רבי יצחק pictures layers of poles, so the load is spread over more people. That means the cluster was even heavier than the earlier calculation.

keyTerms.meaning: Bars of a scale; here, poles resting on other poles

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
bars, and bars upon bars,
phrases.notes: Picture the bars of a balance scale, with upper bars resting on lower ones, so there were more than two poles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the two-pole picture into a stacked arrangement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cluster was carried on layered poles, not just two.

steps.title: Who carried what among the twelve spies
steps.stepSummary: Eight spies carried the cluster, one carried a pomegranate, one a fig, and יהושע and כלב carried nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Eight carried the grape cluster, one carried a pomegranate, and one carried a fig. יהושע and כלב carried nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains his picture by accounting for all twelve spies and what each one carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With stacked poles, eight people shared the cluster, double the four from step 17. The other fruits in the פסוק each took one person. That leaves only יהושע and כלב with empty hands.

phrases.english: How so?
Eight carried the grape cluster,
one carried a pomegranate,
and one carried a fig.
Yehoshua and Calev did not carry anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what רבי יצחק's stacked poles mean in numbers of people.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 8 + 1 + 1 carried, and יהושע and כלב carried nothing

steps.title: Two reasons why יהושע and כלב carried nothing
steps.stepSummary: Either they were too important to carry loads, or they had no part in the spies' bad plan.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because they were important. And if you want, say it is because they were not part of that plan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not ask out loud: why didn't יהושע and כלב help carry? It gives two possible reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is about honor: important people do not carry loads. The second reason is that carrying the fruit was part of the spies' scheme, and יהושע and כלב did not join it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (offers one of two possible answers)

phrases.english: If you want, say it was because they were important.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ בְּאוֹתָהּ עֵצָה.
phrases.english: And if you want, say it was because they were not part of that plan.
phrases.notes: 'That plan' is the spies' plan to frighten the people with the huge fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the detail at the end of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because of their importance, or because they were not part of the spies' plan
steps.whatToRemember: With stacked poles, eight spies carried the cluster. יהושע and כלב carried nothing, either because of their importance or because they stayed out of the spies' plan.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree about the water dispute
steps.stepSummary: A new discussion begins. Two אמוראים disagree about the earlier argument over how high the ירדן water stood, and one begins with רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree about this. One says: according to רבי יהודה's view...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic and introduces a disagreement. This line only sets things up; the actual opinions continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic returns to the earlier dispute about the ירדן crossing. Here the גמרא only names the two אמוראים and starts the first one's words. What he says about רבי יהודה's view comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: One says (in a dispute where we don't specify who)

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha disagree about it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the earlier argument about how high the ירדן water stood when the people crossed.

phrases.english: One says: according to the words of Rabbi Yehuda —

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the grape cluster and returns to the dispute about the ירדן water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a dispute; the content continues on the next amud.
